enemies.name: Byakko Stray (unranked)
enemies.description: Not a member yet. Strays hang around the gang hoping to be noticed, in threes, in tracksuits, at volume.
traits: UNRANKED — beating Strays raises no Heat. Byakko do not count them, and neither should you.
They run the moment the first one goes down.
enemies.tactics: Mob whoever looks smallest, shout a lot, scatter. Use them to show the players the street before the street is dangerous.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Byakko Claw (one stripe)
enemies.description: The bottom rung: one white stripe tattooed on the inside of the left forearm. Claws collect protection money and enforce it.
traits: ONE TRICK — every Claw has exactly one quirk trick. Pick one: a 15-ft shove (STR DC 12), a blinding flash (CON DC 12, blinded 1 round), or a 20-ft standing leap.
enemies.tactics: Fights to win, not to kill. Surrenders cleanly to anyone who beats them cleanly — and then goes and tells a Fang.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Byakko Fang (two stripes)
enemies.description: Two stripes. A Fang runs a block and wants a witness for everything.
traits: SIGNATURE (recharge 5–6) — one real quirk move: 3d8 in a 15-ft cone (DEX DC 13 half), or a grab that restrains (STR DC 13 to escape).
RING-WISE — advantage on saves against being knocked prone.
enemies.tactics: Will not fight in an empty alley. Walks you to a street with people in it, because a win nobody saw does not count.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Byakko Stripe (three stripes)
enemies.description: Three stripes. Holds a street. There are about a dozen of them, and each one got there by beating the last one.
traits: TWO SIGNATURES — give a Stripe two real quirk moves on the Fang pattern, one of them a recharge.
THE LAW — a Stripe fights one challenger at a time if they can. If two PCs engage together, every Byakko member watching stops being an audience and joins in.
enemies.tactics: Arrives with an escort of two Claws who do not fight unless the Law is broken. Offers the challenge by name.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Hazama Ritsu, "Ricochet" (Claw)
enemies.description: Sixteen, skinny, one stripe and desperate for a second. Picks the smallest-looking PC every single time and narrates the whole fight, badly, at volume.
traits: RUBBER JOINTS (reaction, once per round) — when hit in melee, he takes half damage and bounces 15 ft away without provoking.
enemies.tactics: Hit and bounce. Gives up the moment he is cornered — and then follows the PCs home to ask how they did that. A good first Byakko for any table.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Kei & Rei Okita, "the Echo Twins" (Claws)
enemies.description: One preset per twin — run two. Byakko's only pair, and the rest of the gang thinks they are a joke.
traits: ECHO STEP — whatever one twin did on their last turn, the other may do on this one with +2 to hit, and the target has disadvantage on any save against it.
PAIR — they have never met anybody else who fights as two.
enemies.tactics: The 2v2 bracket's mirror. Fought as a pair it is a fair, funny, excellent fight. Fought alone, they take you apart. Either way they will want to know who taught you.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Dōmeki Daigo, "Brick" (Fang)
enemies.description: Runs Swing Town, a batting centre in the Ikebukuro backstreets, and the Ring nights in its back cage. Twenty-four, gentle with the kids who come in to bat, and the Fang most PCs meet first.
traits: BRICKHIDE — resistance to bludgeoning damage.
BRICK WALL (bonus action, recharge 5–6) — until his next turn he cannot be moved, knocked prone or grappled, and anything that hits him in melee takes 1d6.
enemies.tactics: Stands still and lets you hit him, because hitting him hurts. Respects anybody who works out that he hates being made to move.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Saeki Momo, "Hairpin" (Fang)
enemies.description: Ex-sprinter, thrown off her school team for using her quirk on the track. Izuto Kutsu is everything she lost and she will want to race him.
traits: PINCUSHION (recharge 5–6) — 15-ft burst around her, DEX DC 13, 3d6 piercing, half on a save.
TRACK LEGS — can Disengage as a bonus action.

SOMETHING STANDING BEHIND HER (Heat 4+ only) — since spring there has been a figure at her shoulder that she cannot explain and her registry does not list. It is an Envoy, and it is the Astral Court's first trace. See "The Astral Court."
enemies.tactics: Kites. Never stands still. If a PC outruns her, she stops fighting and asks for a rematch on a track.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Ibuki Kōsuke, "Three-Stripe Kō" (Stripe)
enemies.description: Holds Ikebukuro North Alley. Cold, precise, honourable to the letter of the Law, and the owner of a notebook with the name of everyone he has ever beaten.
traits: AFTERIMAGE — begins each fight with two afterimages. While any remain, attacks against him have disadvantage, and any hit or area effect that would touch him pops one instead of dealing damage.
THE COLLECTOR — he has watched the festival archive. He quotes the commentary at you, accurately, and he has read your weakness.
enemies.tactics: The first Byakko who has done his homework. Play the commentary-quoting lightly — it is a schoolyard echo of Appetite, not a scare.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Tsuruoka Fusae, "Madame Tsuru" (Stripe)
enemies.description: Sixty-eight. Runs Lucky Seven, the dice den above a noodle shop, and has held three stripes for thirty-one years because nobody has beaten her yet. Adores Kinji's shoes.

attacks.name: Heavy Hand
attacks.notes: Once per round, the target makes a CON DC 15 save or is stunned until the end of its next turn.

traits: SEEN IT ALL — advantage on saves against being frightened, charmed or tricked, and she cannot be surprised.
THE HOUSE — inside Lucky Seven, every Byakko member present fights for her without being asked.
enemies.tactics: Does not start fights. Ends them, with one slap, and then offers you tea. Would very much like to see what Kinji's quirk does, and has a die she would like him to roll.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Kuze Asagi, the Azure Corner
enemies.description: Holds the east. Twenty-two, a former national-level swimmer, calm to the point of boredom. Masahata Shikoji is the first person in years he has wanted to fight.

attacks.name: Multiattack — two Riptide whips
attacks.notes: A hit pulls the target 15 ft toward him.

traits: TIDECALL — pulls water out of drains, pipes and gutters. While he stands in water, +2 AC.
FLOOD LANE (recharge 5–6) — 60-ft line, DEX DC 16 or 5d8 bludgeoning, knocked prone and pushed 20 ft; half and no push on a save. The line stays flooded.
WEAKNESS — lightning in water. If he takes lightning damage while standing in water, he is stunned until the end of his next turn. Nakaya Emari will find this out.
enemies.tactics: Floods the street first and fights second. Every Corner is named for one of the other three guardian beasts, as a boast: the other gods are Byakko's doormen.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Hōjō Akane, the Vermilion Corner
enemies.description: Holds the south. Nineteen, theatrical, gorgeous, insufferable. Watched Tazato breathe fire at the festival and has been furious about the competition ever since. Rakuka thinks she is the coolest person he has ever seen.
traits: PYRE DIVE (recharge 5–6) — dives on a point within 40 ft: 10-ft radius, DEX DC 16, 6d10 fire, half on a save.
REBIRTH (once per day) — at 0 HP she bursts into flame (3d10 fire to everything within 15 ft, no save) and stands back up with 40 HP.
SHOWWOMAN — will not fight without an audience, and plays to it.
enemies.tactics: Opens from the air and never lands if she can help it. Hates being ignored more than being hit.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Genda Tetsuo, the Black Corner
enemies.description: Holds the north and the front door of the Cage. Forty, enormous, sells takoyaki from a cart, reads philosophy between customers, and has not lost a fight in eleven years.
traits: SHELL — if he has not moved this turn: AC 20 and resistance to all damage except psychic.
IMMOVABLE — cannot be pushed, pulled, knocked prone or grappled by anything smaller than Huge.
DOORMAN — to reach the White Tiger in the Cage, you go through him or you talk your way past him. He is open to both.
enemies.tactics: Plants himself and waits. Thinks Kazama, Setaka and Hiro are the most interesting things to happen to him in a decade, and will happily stop a fight to discuss load-bearing.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Kōga Rin, the Yellow Corner
enemies.description: Holds the centre — the Cage itself — and is the White Tiger's second. Twenty-five, unsmiling, and the fastest thing in west Tokyo until the festival. She has watched Izuto Kutsu's obstacle course run forty times.
traits: STORM STRIDE — never provokes opportunity attacks.
ARC STEP (bonus action) — teleports up to 30 ft along anything conductive: rail, wire, wet ground.
OVERCHARGE — if she is soaked, her next kick deals its lightning damage to her as well.
SECOND — if the White Tiger is in the fight, Rin acts immediately after her.
enemies.tactics: Izuto's rival whether he likes it or not, and Nakaya's too. Never stops moving; hates water.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Hakuro Mitsuki, the White Tiger
enemies.description: Byakko. Twenty-seven, six foot four, a white-tiger heteromorph with black stripes down her arms and gold eyes, undefeated for six years. Eats at the same ramen stall at one in the morning every night. Watched the Sports Festival's paired tournament and thought it was cowardice.
traits: POUNCE — if she moves 20 ft straight at a creature and hits it with a claw, it makes a STR DC 18 save or is knocked prone, and she may bite it as a bonus action.
ROAR (recharge 5–6) — 30-ft cone, WIS DC 18 or frightened for 1 minute (repeat the save at the end of each turn).
APEX READ — after a creature hits her, she has advantage on her next attack against that creature.
UNDEFEATED (2 per round, at the end of another creature's turn) — move up to half her speed without provoking, or make one claw attack.

THE LAW IS THE LAW — she fights one challenger at a time. If a second U.A. student joins in, she steps back and declares the fight void. The way round this is in "The White Tiger," and it is the campaign's thesis.
enemies.tactics: Not a monster, not a villain in the Appetite sense — a champion. She wants the best fight in Tokyo and she thinks the festival winners might be it. Play her with total sincerity.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Legion Thrall
enemies.description: Scarlet Legion. Somebody the Scarlet Legion fed from and did not finish. Grey, slow, silent, always in numbers. Hellsing's ghouls, in a Tokyo dock.

attacks.name: Claw
attacks.notes: On a hit, CON DC 11 or gain a rank of Queasy.

traits: MINDLESS — immune to being charmed or frightened; obeys the nearest Legion vampire.
SUNLIGHT — crumbles to ash at the end of any turn it spends in direct sunlight.
ONCE A PERSON — they were somebody. A private clinic in Minato has the records of who.
enemies.tactics: Six at a time, out of the dark, at the wharf. The horror is that they are slow and do not stop.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Legionary (Scarlet Legion)
enemies.description: Scarlet Legion. A turned vampire of the Legion's rank and file. Often recruited from people who were already strong — some of them used to be Byakko.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: It regains HP equal to the necrotic damage dealt.

traits: REGENERATION — regains 10 HP at the start of its turn unless it took radiant, fire or silver damage since its last turn.
GAZE (action) — one creature within 30 ft, WIS DC 13 or charmed for 1 minute (treats the Legionary as a trusted friend).
MIST (once per night) — becomes mist until its next turn: fly 30 ft, passes through gaps, immune to non-radiant damage.

WEAKNESSES — in direct sunlight: no regeneration, 4d6 radiant at the start of each turn, disadvantage on everything. Vulnerable to radiant and silver. Cannot enter a private home uninvited. Cannot cross running water unaided.
enemies.tactics: Claw then bite, every turn, on the same target. Ren Suzuki's beam is radiant — the Legion will know what that means before he does.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Mina Toda, Centurion of the Scarlet Legion
enemies.description: Scarlet Legion. Looks nineteen. Has looked nineteen since 1923. The Legion's diplomat and recruiter, and almost certainly the first of them a PC ever speaks to — at a party, holding a glass of something red she does not drink.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: She regains HP equal to the necrotic damage.

traits: REGENERATION 15 — as a Legionary.
GAZE — WIS DC 15.

RESTRICTION RELEASE (bonus action) — she fights sealed at Level Three. Each release (Three → Two → One) gives +2 to hit and damage and 20 temporary HP, and makes her stranger to look at: by Level One her shadow has eyes in it.
WEAKNESSES — as a Legionary.
enemies.tactics: Talks first, always. Would much rather recruit a PC than fight one, and is honest about what the offer costs, which is the frightening part.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Captain Grau, Centurion of the Scarlet Legion
enemies.description: Scarlet Legion. The Legion's soldier. Seven feet, grey greatcoat, has not spoken since 1945. The Legion sends Grau when talking has failed.
traits: REGENERATION 15 — as a Legionary.
UNBROKEN — the first time each night he would drop to 0 HP, he drops to 1 instead.
RESTRICTION RELEASE — as Mina Toda.
WEAKNESSES — as a Legionary.
enemies.tactics: Walks forward. Hits whatever is in front of him. Stops when told to.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Lady Akabane Seraphine, Legate of the Scarlet Legion
enemies.description: Scarlet Legion. Four hundred years old, looks thirty, runs the Legion from the Crimson Room in Ginza. Unfailingly courteous. Has outlived eleven generations of heroes and considers hero society a phase.
traits: REGENERATION 25.
GAZE — every creature of her choice within 30 ft, WIS DC 19.
LEVEL ZERO (once) — she stops being a person-shaped thing, and four shadow hounds step out of her coat (AC 15, 30 HP, bite +10 for 2d10+5).
NOT A FIGHT — she is beyond the party at any level this campaign reaches. She is a negotiation, and the campaign treats her as one.
enemies.tactics: She does not fight students. She invites them to dinner, and the danger is in what she offers.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Daybreak Initiate (Astral Court)
enemies.description: Astral Court. A first-rung student of Sunbreath. Registered Quirkless, and proud of it. Trained in a bathhouse.
traits: SUNBREATH (3 per short rest) — add 1d6 radiant to a hit; or walk on water or up a wall until the end of the turn; or heal 1d8 by touch. Against a Legion vampire the heal deals 2d8 radiant instead.
BREATH IS EVERYTHING — gagged, choked or underwater without a breath, Sunbreath stops working.
enemies.tactics: Defensive, polite, and absolutely certain the PCs are about to be eaten by something.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Hōshō Kaito & PAPER PLANES (Envoy-bearer)
enemies.description: Astral Court. Seventeen, night clerk at a Kōenji convenience store, magnificent pompadour, extremely polite until you mention his hair.
traits: ENVOY: PAPER PLANES — Power B · Speed B · Range D · Durability C · Precision B · Potential A. Anything it punches folds like paper for one minute: a door becomes a crane, a car folds flat, a wall folds open. A creature it hits makes a CON DC 14 save or is folded flat (incapacitated, speed 0) until the end of its next turn.
ENVOY RULES — an Envoy can only be hurt by another Envoy or by radiant damage, and damage dealt to it is dealt to its bearer. Hit Kaito.
SUNBREATH (4 per short rest).
enemies.tactics: A good kid who has been fighting a war nobody told him was optional. The likeliest Court friend for the class.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Grandmother Hinata Sae, Elder of the Astral Court
enemies.description: Astral Court. Eighty-one, runs the Matsu-no-Yu bathhouse in Kōenji. The rumour is that she can stay underwater for ten minutes. The rumour is wrong. It is twelve.
traits: SUNBREATH (unlimited).
OVERDRIVE (recharge 5–6) — a 30-ft line of sunlight carried through water or metal: DEX DC 17, 8d8 radiant. Legion vampires save at disadvantage and take double.
NO ENVOY — she never wanted one. She has buried three students who did.
enemies.tactics: She will test a PC, not fight one: a slap that hurts like sunburn, and then a question about how they breathe.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Saotome Shin & BAD MOON, the Arrowhead Thief
enemies.description: Astral Court. Thirty-four, a former Courtier who believes Envoys should belong to the strong. Byakko's ladder of power is his idea of heaven, and he has been feeding it.

attacks.name: The Arrowhead
attacks.notes: CON DC 16. Success: the target awakens an Envoy within the week. Failure: it drops to 0 HP and begins dying.

traits: ENVOY: BAD MOON — Power B · Speed C · Range C · Durability A · Precision C · Potential E. ECLIPSE: within 30 ft of Bad Moon, light sources go out and radiant damage and Sunbreath stop working.
ENVOY RULES — as Hōshō Kaito.
He has been cutting Byakko fighters with a stolen arrowhead since spring. Saeki Momo is one of the ones who lived.
enemies.tactics: The Court storyline's villain if you want one. Fights from inside his Eclipse so that nothing the Court taught can touch him.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Kegare, Grade Four
enemies.description: Kuroshiki. A knot of somebody's fear that has learned to move. A thing in a stairwell. Mostly harmless. Mostly.
traits: UNSEEN — invisible to anybody without Sumi, and it does not appear on cameras.
BORN OF DREAD — resistance to all damage except radiant and Sumi-infused attacks.
enemies.tactics: They gather where people have been afraid: hospitals, crime scenes, every place Appetite has ever been.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Kegare, Grade Two
enemies.description: Kuroshiki. Big enough to be a problem and old enough to talk. It speaks in the voice of whatever fear made it.
traits: UNSEEN and BORN OF DREAD — as Grade Four.
DREAD (recharge 5–6) — every creature within 30 ft that can perceive it makes a WIS DC 14 save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.
FEAR FEEDS IT — whenever a creature within 30 ft fails a save against being frightened, it regains 10 HP.
enemies.tactics: Picks the most frightened person in the room and stays on them.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Kegare, Grade One — "the Roll Call"
enemies.description: Kuroshiki. Born in the Heights Alliance ground-floor corridor out of a class that lost somebody. It counts.
traits: UNSEEN and BORN OF DREAD — as Grade Four.

COUNTING — at the start of each round it counts the people in the room aloud, in the voice of whoever started the roll call in the loading yard, and loses its place, and starts again. Every creature that hears it makes a WIS DC 17 save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.
FED — it regains 15 HP whenever a creature within 60 ft fails a save against being frightened.
enemies.tactics: Run it only if the table has the appetite — see the safety note in "The Thing in the Laundry Room." It is beaten by people who refuse to be counted: anybody who answers the count out loud with their own name is immune to Counting for the rest of the fight.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Mibu Tsubaki, Kuroshiki sorcerer (Grade Two)
enemies.description: Kuroshiki. Sixteen, prickly, the Mibu house's best student in a generation and painfully aware of it. Hunts in a pair, like every Kuroshiki: "one to see, one to cut."
traits: SUMI (8 per long rest).
MIBU BLOOD RITE — Red Bind (bonus action, 1 Sumi): STR DC 15 or restrained. Clot (reaction, 2 Sumi): halve the damage of one hit.
VEIL (action, 2 Sumi) — a black dome up to 100 ft across. From outside, nothing is happening, and cameras record an empty street.
PACT (once per fight) — she declares a restriction aloud ("I will not move from this spot") and gains +2 to her save DC and +1d10 on Blood Lance while she keeps it.
enemies.tactics: Will tell U.A. students to go home, twice, and then need their help.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Kagura Ichirō, Kuroshiki sorcerer (Grade Two)
enemies.description: Kuroshiki. Seventeen, sleepy, polite, and Tsubaki's partner since they were nine. He does the seeing; she does the cutting.
traits: SUMI (8 per long rest).
KAGURA SHADOW RITE — Hound (bonus action, 2 Sumi): a shadow hound forms from his hand-shadow (AC 13, 25 HP), lasting 1 minute; at most two.
THE ONE WHO SEES — he can see Kegare from a mile away and always knows where the nearest one is.
enemies.tactics: Stays behind Tsubaki and points. Gets on quietly well with Kibi Kankei, for reasons neither of them examines.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Shirasagi Rei, unranked Kuroshiki sorcerer
enemies.description: Kuroshiki. Twenty-eight, heir of the Shirasagi house, wears sunglasses indoors, extraordinarily strong and extraordinarily annoying about it. Teaches at the Kurama Rite School. Thinks Ando Iorai's sunglasses show good character.
traits: THE LONG WAY ROUND — he can make the distance between himself and anything he chooses impossible to cross. Attacks against him do not arrive unless he allows them to.

ENCLOSURE: THE LONG CORRIDOR (once per day) — a 60-ft sphere; every creature inside is walking down an endless corridor toward him and is incapacitated for 1 minute (WIS DC 20 at the end of each turn).
NOT A FIGHT — like the Legate, he is beyond this campaign. He is a mentor, a warning, and a very irritating lunch.
enemies.tactics: Never fights the class. Shows up, makes an enormous problem disappear in one move, eats somebody's snack, and leaves.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours on the campaign's three-tier scale.

enemies.name: Nagira Sou, "Pylon" (Claw)
enemies.description: Seventeen, holds the laundrette corner, makes himself heavy enough to be immovable and hates every part of his job except that. Apologises before and after.
traits: DEADWEIGHT (bonus action) — until his next turn he cannot be moved, pushed or knocked prone by anything short of Huge, and his speed is 0.
enemies.tactics: Plants himself in a doorway so nobody can get past, which is the entire extent of his ambition. Will stand aside if asked nicely, and then be in trouble for it.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Tobe Miyu, "Tally" (Claw)
enemies.description: Sixteen, one stripe, earned with a chair in front of nine witnesses. Keeps the gang’s books in three exercise books and a phone. Not a fight — a conversation.

attacks.name: A chair
attacks.notes: She is not a fighter and the stat block is a formality.

traits: THE BOOKS — she knows what every member of Byakko is owed, owes and is worth, and where the money goes, and she has never shown anybody.
NOT A FIGHT — the most useful non-combatant in the backstreets.
enemies.tactics: Talk to her. Everything in "the turf economy" is in her exercise books, and she will trade it for help with a problem that has nothing to do with the gang.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Ōkawachi Jin, "Dropkick" (Claw)
enemies.description: Eighteen, challenges upward constantly, loses constantly, undeterred. The reason rule six exists.

attacks.name: Flying kick
attacks.notes: If he moved 20 ft first, add 1d8 — and he lands prone, every time, without fail.

traits: UNDETERRED — he fights until he is unconscious and is cheerful about it the next day.
enemies.tactics: Announce him. Have him challenge the most famous PC in the street in front of everybody, lose in two rounds, and come back next window.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Murase Kotoha, "Nettle" (Fang)
enemies.description: Nineteen, holds the noodle bar’s street, personally enforces rule four. Kind to the unstriped kids and frightening to everybody else.

attacks.name: Nettle (recharge 5–6)
attacks.notes: CON DC 13; half and no condition on a save. On a failure, poisoned until the end of its next turn.

traits: RULE FOUR — anybody who threatens the noodle bar or an unstriped kid in her presence gets her full attention, and nothing else does.
enemies.tactics: The Byakko most likely to end up helping the class, which she will deny. Fight her once and she is a contact for the rest of the campaign.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Yanagi Daichi, "Half-Step" (Fang)
enemies.description: Twenty-one, the gang’s teacher and the best pure technician in two wards. Failed the U.A. entrance exam twice at fifteen and never mentions it.
traits: HALF-STEP — once per round, as a reaction to being targeted by a melee attack, he moves 5 ft and the attack misses.
HE HAS WATCHED YOUR MATCH, AND NOT ON CLEAN READ — he watched the broadcast, twice, because he loves it. He will tell a PC what they did well, specifically, and he will be right.
enemies.tactics: A spar, not a fight. Honourable, delighted, and the most generous opponent in the campaign. Bose would have him tomorrow and the table should feel that.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Imai Tatsuhiko, "Sandbag" (Fang)
enemies.description: Twenty, runs the Ring’s betting book out of Swing Town’s back office. Knows what everybody is worth to the yen. The first member of Byakko to buy a Clean Read page.
traits: SOAK — the first 10 damage from each attack against him is reduced to half. He has been hit for a living for four years.

THE BOOK — quotes odds on the PCs to their faces and sells information about any fighter in two wards. In Chapter 7 he is the first to work out what Clean Read means for the Stripe Law, and he is frightened by it, and he is right to be.
enemies.tactics: A businessman who can take a punch. Would much rather have the class’s custom than their blood.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Kōno Sae, "Hinge" (Stripe)
enemies.description: Twenty-four, holds the chop shop, opens any lock by touch. The Stripe who sold a man with a scar a white van for cash in the spring and watched him bleed on the counter.

attacks.name: Unhinge (recharge 5–6)
attacks.notes: One creature wearing armour or carrying a weapon: STR DC 14 or it comes apart and falls to the ground.

traits: HINGE (action) — she touches any lock, door, restraint, panel or joint and it opens. Any of them. Including a cell, a cold-store hatch, or handcuffs on somebody else.
THE VAN — she remembers him exactly and will describe him once, properly, to anybody who asks properly. That is the whole of the Appetite connection and it should never be more.
enemies.tactics: Professional, bored, and completely willing to be arrested, which nobody expects. She will not resist.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Fukami Ryōta, "Ladder" (Stripe)
enemies.description: Twenty-six, holds the Shinjuku west-exit alleys, and recruits. Finds the fourteen-year-olds on the crash barriers and gives them somewhere to belong. The most dangerous man in Byakko, and he has never hurt anybody in his life.

attacks.name: Climb with me (once per fight)
attacks.notes: One creature that can hear him: WIS DC 15 or it cannot attack him until the end of its next turn. He is not charming them — he is telling them, sincerely, that they are better than this street.

traits: EVERY SINGLE THING HE SAYS to an unstriped fourteen-year-old is something U.A. said to the class in Chapter 1.
enemies.tactics: Warm. Genuinely warm. He believes he is doing those kids a favour, and for about a third of them he is.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Sawaguchi Hidemi, "Quiet" (Stripe)
enemies.description: Thirty-three, holds the hospital street, murmurs, patches up every fighter in the backstreets and asks nothing. A nurse for eleven years first. The Scarlet Legion’s loudest trace in the city.

attacks.name: Multiattack — two pressure strikes
attacks.notes: CON DC 15 or disadvantage on its next attack.

attacks.name: Field dressing (3/day)
attacks.notes: She will use these on the PCs, in a fight, without being asked, if somebody is badly hurt.

traits: THE GREY ONES — since spring she has treated four Claws who turned up pale, slow and missing a night, with two neat marks on the neck, and she stopped asking. Nobody has ever talked to her about it.
enemies.tactics: Barely a fight at all; she would rather treat than hit. If the class are kind to her once, she is the Underground’s best doorway and does not know it.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Amano Keita, "Footnote" (four stripes)
enemies.description: Nineteen. A Stray eight months ago. His quirk lets him stand up once. He has beaten a Claw, two Fangs, Three-Stripe Kō and Saeki Momo, every one of them by knowing exactly what they could not do.

attacks.name: Multiattack — two plain strikes
attacks.notes: No quirk in them at all.

traits: PREPARED FOR YOU (once per round) — he names, out loud and accurately, one thing a target’s quirk cannot do, read off a teardown he watched before the fight, and gains advantage on his next attack roll against them. Say the actual limitation from the PC’s sheet.
SECOND WIND — the first time he drops to 0 HP, he stands back up with 25.

FOOTWORK, NOTHING ELSE — no signature move at all. Any creature that uses a technique, training benefit or Underground gift that has never been filmed strips Prepared For You for the rest of the fight, against everybody. Do not tell the players this.
enemies.tactics: Polite, apologetic, and genuinely puzzled that anybody minds. He did not break the Law; he read it. See Chapter 7, "A Challenge, Bought and Paid For."
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Arrear, one month overdue
enemies.description: The Ledger. Somebody who was not collected on time and has been standing where they were told to stand for five weeks. Still mostly shaped like a person, which is worse.
traits: OVERDUE — quirk damage is halved against it. Radiant damage, Sumi-infused attacks and writs hurt it fully.
WAITING — it cannot willingly move more than 30 ft from the spot it was told to wait in, and it will not pursue. It also will not stop.
enemies.tactics: It does not hunt. It stands in a stairwell, or under a barrier, or at the back of a hospital car park, and anybody who comes within reach is within reach.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Arrear, one year overdue
enemies.description: The Ledger. Twelve months of standing still. It has stopped having a face and started having a direction.

attacks.name: Still due (recharge 5–6)
attacks.notes: It says the date it was supposed to be collected on. WIS DC 13 or frightened until the end of its next turn.

traits: OVERDUE — quirk damage halved; radiant, Sumi and writs hurt it fully.
WAITING — 30 ft from its spot, no pursuit, no stopping.
enemies.tactics: Immobile, relentless, and loud about one number. The fight is a positioning puzzle, not a chase.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Arrear, nine months overdue ("the one under the barrier")
enemies.description: The Ledger. The Yanaka level crossing. Nine months in the four inches under the barrier arm, because the Rite calls it a Kegare and the Ledger calls it an Arrear and nobody will sign. Chapter 8’s Contact encounter.

attacks.name: Four minutes (start of each round)
attacks.notes: The barriers come down. Everything within 20 ft of the rails is pushed 10 ft toward the crossing (STR DC 15 to resist), then a train goes over, then they go up.

traits: BOTH AND NEITHER — it is an Arrear and a Kegare at once. Unseen without Sumi or a Mark, Born of Dread, and Overdue, and the three rules stack, which is exactly why nobody has dealt with it.
WAITING — it will not leave the crossing under any circumstances, including to save itself.
enemies.tactics: Not a hard fight for a party at level 11; a strange one. Two wardens will watch and will not help, and will be helpful about it.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Arrear, a century overdue
enemies.description: The Ledger. A hundred and ten years at the back of a building that was knocked down in 1962. There is no person left in it and there is still a date.

attacks.name: The wrong date (recharge 5–6)
attacks.notes: WIS DC 18 or 6d8 psychic and frightened 1 minute; half and no fear on a save. A creature that answers with its own name is immune to The Wrong Date for the rest of the fight.

traits: OVERDUE, and BORN OF DREAD if you want it both ways.
WAITING, STILL — a 60-ft radius it has not left since the Occupation. Inside it, advantage on everything. Outside it, it cannot go.
enemies.tactics: Only if a third season wants it. The Ledger’s version of the Roll Call: beaten by people who refuse to be a number, and by nothing else.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Hibino Asa, Runner of the Ninth Round
enemies.description: The Ledger. Fifteen, and has been fifteen since 1998. A satchel, a bicycle, a pencil she licks, and the best records in the department. No writ — Runners do not get one, and she has asked four times.

attacks.name: Notice
attacks.notes: She hits people with a rolled-up form. It works better than it should.

attacks.name: A Mark (action, once per day)
attacks.notes: She inks a character on the back of a willing creature’s hand: they see wardens, writs and Arrears permanently. It costs them a page, and she explains that clearly first, every time.

traits: FILED — a warden on duty does not appear on any camera, and anybody without a Mark, a Sumi pool or recent proximity to their own death sees only a person in black they will not remember. Quirk attacks still hit her perfectly well.
THE ROUND — she knows where every Arrear in her district is standing, and how long it has been there, and will tell anybody who asks politely.

NOT A FIGHT — the friendliest thing in the Underground, and the most upsetting: four of the Case 9 names are in her notebook with ticks against them, filed correctly, and she would like to know whether there was a problem with it.
enemies.tactics: Cheerful, chatty, and relieved to have somebody to talk to. Deliver the notebook flatly and then say nothing.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Kajiura, Hand of the Fourth Desk
enemies.description: The Ledger. Seven feet, black uniform, a writ called Second Frost, and a Desk above him that has been vacant since 1945 — which means his countersignatures come from nowhere and most of his authority is theoretical.

attacks.name: Writ: Second Frost
attacks.notes: Hurts an Arrear or a Kegare fully.

attacks.name: First Reading (once per fight)
attacks.notes: "Second Frost, settle." DEX DC 16 or 4d10 cold and speed 0 until the end of its next turn.

traits: FILED — as Hibino Asa.

NO COUNTERSIGNATURE — he will not draw Second Frost outside his jurisdiction, and almost nothing in Tokyo is inside it. He is a CR 9 stat block standing perfectly still with his hands at his sides, and that is not a bug.
WITH A COUNTERSIGNATURE — forged, granted, or signed by a PC who did not read the form — he is the best ally in the Underground and ends most fights in two rounds.
enemies.tactics: One sentence per scene, maximum, and always a procedural observation. The sentence he says when a PC is about to die is the most useful thing anybody says all chapter.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Shirouzu Genbei, struck off
enemies.description: The Ledger. Struck off in 1954 for a countersignature he wrote himself. Runs a sweet shop in Yanaka, three streets from the crossing. Was a Desk. Still writes like one. Not a fight.

attacks.name: Writ: Long Summer
attacks.notes: It still answers to him, which is technically theft.

traits: STRUCK OFF — he is not Filed. Cameras see him. He pays tax. He finds this hilarious.

A COUNTERSIGNATURE, FORGED (ritual, one hour) — indistinguishable from a real one. His price is never money: a favour, an errand, a true answer to a question he asks, or a jar of something from the Astral Court’s bathhouse.
NOT A FIGHT — the Ledger’s way in and its only sympathetic authority.
enemies.tactics: Delighted to see visitors. Sells them something cheap first. Tells them the truth in the wrong order.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Tōno Shigemori, the First Desk
enemies.description: The Ledger. Holds the book. Everybody in the city is in it, on a page, with a date, and the dates are not wrong. Unfailingly polite, entirely without malice, and the least negotiable thing in this campaign. Not a fight.
traits: SECOND READING: THE DEPARTMENT (once) — a 120-ft radius becomes his jurisdiction. Inside it he cannot be surprised or moved, no creature may take the Dash action, and every creature hears its own page read out.
ONE QUESTION — he will answer exactly one question truthfully, to anybody who reaches him. The price is a page with their name on it, and he will say so, and he will not show them the date.
NOT A FIGHT — like the Legate and Shirasagi Rei, beyond any level this module reaches. He is a negotiation.
enemies.tactics: He does not threaten and he does not bargain. He has an appointment at eleven. The horror is entirely in how reasonable he is about the price.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Miyashita Gō, "Tenpin"
enemies.description: Fifty-one, a C-rank villain with nine previous convictions and a kinetic quirk that puts a standing target down and keeps it down. Has never beaten anybody good in his life. Subscribed to Clean Read in February and has beaten four licensed heroes since.

attacks.name: Multiattack — two strikes
attacks.notes: On a hit, STR DC 15 or knocked prone.

attacks.name: Split (recharge 5–6)
attacks.notes: DEX DC 15, pushed 20 ft and prone; half and no push on a save.

traits: READ AHEAD (once per round) — he names one thing a target’s quirk cannot do, accurately, from the video playing on the phone clipped to his jacket, and gains advantage on his next attack roll against them. Read the real limitation off the PC’s sheet.
KEEPS THEM DOWN — advantage on attacks against prone creatures, and he does not let them up.
enemies.tactics: Not clever and not fast, and he knows exactly what each of them cannot do. Surrenders the moment it goes badly and then talks, helpfully, at length, and gives the class Ebata Kyōsuke’s name.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Tokieda Mei, first year
enemies.description: Fifteen, 1-A, Replay. Enormously polite, relentless, and has built a fighting style entirely out of somebody else’s footage. An ally and a liability, usually at once.

attacks.name: Borrowed opening
attacks.notes: Damage type as whatever she is copying.

traits: REPLAY — once per fight she repeats her own last action exactly, including the parts she does not understand.
SHE FIGHTS LIKE SOMEBODY ELSE — she uses a PC’s signature opening at the wrong moment, and it does not fit her body, and it will not, and she has not worked that out.
WILL NOT GO DOWN — at 0 HP she is unconscious and stable, never dying. The module does not kill her.
enemies.tactics: In the car park she is up and losing and still going, because she copied somebody who does not stop. A PC who tells her to get out has to actually make her.
enemies.stats_source: Written for The Shortlist: After Hours, second season (Chapters 7–8).

enemies.name: Yuka Ōba
enemies.description: Thirty-eight, a cardigan, a nine-page printout she paid ¥18,000 for, no combat training of any kind, and a real grievance about a real hero that nobody would look at. She is going to try.

attacks.name: She hits somebody with a bag

traits: WARP (3/day) — her quirk moves a held object three feet to the left. It is on a form. It is useless. She has read nine pages about how to use it on a sixteen-year-old and one of the nine pages is right.
SHE WILL NOT STOP — no save against being frightened and no interest in one.
THE HARDEST FIGHT IN THE CHAPTER — because hitting her is monstrous, because she is correct about the hero, and because she came to a karaoke booth in Shinjuku since it was the only door that opened.
enemies.tactics: First customer in "The Market." Do not make her dangerous and do not make her ridiculous. Let the class work out that the problem is not her.

enemies.name: A co-ordinated package (one of three)
enemies.description: ¥60,000 bought three people one plan built around one real limitation, and they have rehearsed it, and they get to four minutes forty. Run three of these.

attacks.name: Multiattack — two strikes
attacks.notes: Damage type to taste; give each of the three a different element.

traits: THE PLAN — while at least two of them are within 30 ft of each other, each has advantage on attacks against the target the package was bought for.
FOUR MINUTES FORTY — at the start of round five, if the fight is still going, they all gain 20 temporary HP and say so out loud.
enemies.tactics: In a stairwell at Nakano station, because the plan needs a corridor. Break up the trio and the plan collapses entirely.

enemies.name: The last customer
enemies.description: She did not buy a teardown of a student. She bought forty minutes on Saki Hiyori, 2.3 million views, ¥400,000, and she is a professional with a three-year grudge, and four second-years are in the road.
traits: PREPARED FOR HER, NOT FOR YOU — she has no teardown of any PC and does not want one. The class are an obstacle, and she will walk away from them if they let her.
FORTY MINUTES OF HOMEWORK — against Saki Hiyori specifically she has advantage on all attacks and saves, and she knows the exact shape of Burst.
DISENGAGE AS A BONUS ACTION — she is not here for a brawl.
enemies.tactics: Professional, unhurried, uninterested, and dangerous to a party at level 12 only because she is trying to get past them. If the table needs her, let Creed arrive at the end of round three, absolutely furious about the whole business.

enemies.name: Ebata Kyōsuke (not a fight)
enemies.description: Forty-five, Room 9 of a karaoke place off Shinjuku’s east exit, after eight, cash only. A former fight analyst made redundant in 2021. Quirk: Legible — he reads footage faster than a person should. Registered. Unremarked.
traits: HE DOES NOT DEFEND HIMSELF — if the class attack him he lets them, presses charges, and ends somebody’s provisional licence, and Sugitsu will not be able to fix it.

WHAT HE GIVES THEM — "If you lot ever get to say something first, over the top of your own footage — say the thing the commentary got wrong. Not the weakness. The reason. Nobody’s ever put a reason in the archive."
enemies.tactics: Courteous, unhurried, and not a sophist. A middle-aged man doing lawful work that hurts children, who knows the second half of that and has decided it is not his half.
